name: Playstation 3 Controller
longdesc: The DualShock 3 was Sony's standard controller for the PS3 and is notable for introducing wireless Bluetooth connectivity and Sixaxis motion controls while maintaining the classic PlayStation form factor. It features pressure-sensitive buttons, dual analog sticks, and a built-in rechargeable battery. Although basic by modern standards, it provides a nostalgic feel and works well for retro or classic game collections. New, sealed units are rare and expensive in 2025, but refurbished or third-party versions are more accessible.
tags: Black, Playstation, Three, Controller, Classic, Motion

name: Playstation 4 Controller
longdesc: The DualShock 4 was a major upgrade from its predecessor, with a more ergonomic design, a clickable touchpad, an integrated speaker, and a light bar used for in-game feedback and PlayStation Camera tracking. It also includes a 3.5mm audio jack and improved analog sticks with tighter resistance. This controller is widely used even in PC gaming, thanks to its plug-and-play compatibility and Bluetooth support. It remains very relevant in 2025, especially for PS4 and backward-compatible PS5 titles.
tags: White, Playstation, Four, Controller, Touchpad, Light bar

name: Playstation 5 Controller
longdesc: Sonys DualSense is a standout next-gen controller packed with innovative features. It offers highly immersive haptic feedback and adaptive triggers that provide dynamic resistance, simulating everything from drawing a bowstring to braking a vehicle. The controller also sports a built-in microphone, advanced motion sensors, a more comfortable grip, and a USB-C charging port. It's widely considered one of the best modern game controllers due to its blend of cutting-edge tech and comfort.
tags: White, Playstation, Five, Controller, Haptics, Adaptive triggers, Modern

name: Switch Pro Controller
longdesc: Nintendos Pro Controller for the Switch 2 builds on the success of the original with new features for modern gaming. It now includes GL/GR back buttons (rear paddles), a 3.5mm headphone jack, and a new C button for expanded input. The controller is designed with a large, comfortable grip, precise analog sticks, and motion controls. Its ideal for traditional console games that require more precision and longer playtime than the Joy-Cons can comfortably provide.
tags: Black, Nintendo, Pro, Controller, Comfortable, Motion

name: Xbox 360 Controller
longdesc: Regarded as one of the best-designed controllers of its generation, the Xbox 360 controller set a new standard for comfort and responsiveness. It features a familiar layout with offset analog sticks, a responsive D-pad, and pressure-sensitive triggers. It lacks Bluetooth and instead uses a proprietary wireless connection, though wired versions are also available. While no longer in production, it's still used by retro enthusiasts and works well on PCs with the right adapters.

name: Xbox One Controller
longdesc: This controller refined the 360s design with improved ergonomics, textured grips, and a more reliable D-pad. It introduced a better trigger response and later revisions included Bluetooth for easy wireless use on PCs and mobile devices. The design feels premium without going overboard on features, making it a reliable, go-to controller for many gamers. It remains fully compatible with the Xbox Series X|S and is still manufactured in multiple colors.
tags: White, Xbox, One, Controller, Textured Grip

name: Xbox Elite Controller
longdesc: A premium controller aimed at competitive gamers, the Elite Series 2 allows nearly every part of its layout to be customized. It features adjustable-tension thumbsticks, swappable D-pads and paddles, hair-trigger locks, and up to three custom profiles. The built-in battery charges via USB-C or the included charging dock. It’s built with durability and performance in mind and is ideal for serious or professional-level players.
tags: White, Xbox, One, Elite, Controller, Pro-grade, Customizable, Premium

name: Xbox Series Controller
longdesc: This is Microsofts latest standard controller, offering subtle but effective refinements. It includes a hybrid D-pad inspired by the Elite controller, textured triggers and bumpers, and a dedicated Share button for capturing gameplay. It also uses a USB-C port for wired connections and rechargeable battery packs. While not a radical departure, it’s a highly polished update that enhances comfort and precision for long gaming sessions.
